chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Fadl Abu al-Abbas, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two parents and two sisters (from one father and one mother): do they block the mother from receiving one-third? He said, 'No.' I said, 'And three?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'And four?' He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: How many sisters are required to block the mother from receiving her one-third share in inheritance?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific numerical threshold for the 'hijab' (blocking) of the mother’s one-third share by female siblings. While two or three sisters do not prevent the mother from receiving her fixed portion, the presence of four or more sisters blocks her, a ruling that highlights the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between partial and total exclusion in inheritance distribution. This specific condition underscores the dynamic nature of the mother's share, which fluctuates based on the presence of descendants or ascendants, as well as the number of siblings in this particular scenario.
